newsitem.title: USA: Mass. takes out two more tolls on Turnpike.
newsitem.headline: Mass. takes out two more tolls on Turnpike.

text.p: Massachusetts on Wednesday said it had taken out more two toll booths on the western part of state turnpike, which should save motorists about $2 million a year.
The state in July eliminated tollbooths at four other exits, which is anticipated to cost the state about $14 million a year in revenues.
The latest move follows a series of measures to reduce the Turnpike's expenses, including trimming severance and cutting the use of consultants.
"Our mission is to aggressively cut operating costs while finding creative ways to raise revenues," said the chairman of the Turnpike, James Kerasiotes.
Starting on Sunday, September 29, motorists will be able to drive 50 miles on the Turnpike without paying tolls.
